  You are revising ADR-0018 at D:/the-synaptic-sea-2d/docs/architecture/adr-0018-shadow-origin-and-beam-occlusion-consistency.md (project D:/the-synaptic-sea-2d, Godot 4.7.2 GDScript) after per-ADR engine and TD-ADR reviews and a cross-ADR adjudication of the Core tier.   ADR-0018 review verdict ACCEPT-WITH-AMENDMENTS. No blocking engine finding. The GDScript in the ADR compiles and runs on 4.7.2 (headless probe, below). No deprecated or post-cutoff API is used, and none of the 4.7 hazards you listed (typed-return override, packed-array element-write setters, Object-method name clashes, const of a constructed object) occurs. The weak point is the engine evidence for rung B. The "probed" claims are plausible: the five scratch scripts p1.gd to p5.gd exist, and their contents match P-1 to P-12 (size_2d_override, snap_2d, PCF13, CULL_CLOCKWISE). But P-9 and P-10 used a 1200x1200 centred light texture, so they never exercise the engine's culling of occluders by the light's quad extent (E2). The Compatibility cross-check could not be confirmed from the scripts (p1 to p5 contain no compat strings), so treat it as the ADR's word. The headless probe I ran covered API shape only; drawing behaviour is UNVERIFIED because headless uses the dummy renderer. Probe sources are in C:/Users/dasbl/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/adr-probes/review-ADR-0018/.:
  E1 [medium] `offset` is not a `Light2D` property. Probed on 4.7.2: Light2D's own properties are enabled, editor_only, color, energy, blend_mode, range_*, shadow_enabled, shadow_color, shadow_filter, shadow_filter_smooth and shadow_item_cull_mask. `texture`, `offset`, `texture_scale` and `height` belong to `PointLight2D`; `DirectionalLight2D` has only `height` and `max_distance`. The ADR says 'Light2D.offset' throughout (Summary, § 1(b), SHO-02, F2 'a Light2D offset', the 'every hard-shaped light' rule). An offset writer typed `Light2D` will not parse the property statically and fails at run time on the abstract type. `put_light_origin(node: Light2D, ...)` is fine, because it uses only `position`, and the snippet compiled and ran (pos 10.5, -2.5).
    amendment: Say 'PointLight2D.offset' everywhere. Type `beam_offset_writer.gd` parameters as `PointLight2D`. State that every hard-shaped (textured) light is a PointLight2D and a DirectionalLight2D never goes through `BeamOffset`. Keep `put_light_origin(node: Light2D, ...)` as written; it is valid because it only touches `position`.
  E2 [high] Untested engine behaviour that could break rung B: culling of occluders by the light's texture-quad extent. The ADR itself leaves this open (OQ-E, § 4.4). My recollection of the 4.x canvas renderer is that occluders are attached to a light only if their AABB intersects the light's quad (rect_cache, which includes `offset` and `texture_scale`). I could not verify this headless. If it is true, B is exactly the wrong geometry: the node (shadow origin) is at the foot, the quad is moved up to the chest apex and, for a cone texture whose apex is on its edge, extends away from the foot. A wall that lies between foot and chest (the s = 10 to 33 AC-57 rows) then lies outside the quad and casts no shadow, so the beam would light through it while the simulation says blocked. P-9 and P-10 did not test this. The scratch scripts show `_wh_tex(1200)` (a 1200x1200 white square) centred on the node, so the foot and every occluder were always inside the quad. The 100x100 texture in P-2 was used only for the offset-frame check, not for shadows. The 'Positive' claim that 'the probes already show B passing' therefore overstates what is known. `OCC_MARGIN_PX` cannot fix this, because it widens the set the builder emits, not the engine's per-light cull.
    amendment: (a) Reword Consequences and § 5 so P-9 is evidence for the origin and lattice only, not for B on real textures. (b) Add probe SO-P10: shadow-casting beam with the real LO-15 edge-apex texture at shipped scale, rotated through 8 aims, walls placed (i) between foot and chest, (ii) inside the quad, (iii) outside the quad but between the foot and the lit region; pass is zero radius-2 mismatches and no light-through-wall pixel. (c) Make SO-P7 and SO-P9 use the shipping texture, not the centred 1200x1200 one. (d) Pre-register the fallback if SO-P10 fails: pad the beam texture with transparent texels so the quad contains the foot and the occluders of § 4.4 (cost: texture memory, larger quad overdraw), tried before A or D. (e) Correct § 4.4 so the reach-set rule is stated as necessary but not sufficient.
  E3 [medium] § 3.1 extends `put_light_origin` and the shadow rule to every light, but the black-screen hazard from P-4 is only discussed for the beam foot. With `CULL_DISABLED` a shadow-casting light whose origin lies inside a closed occluder polygon renders the whole view dark (P-4: luminance 0.00). The beam foot is outside every footprint by construction, but a beacon, a lent fixture or a wall lamp anchored on a floor-plane anchor in or next to an OCCLUDES_LIGHT rectangle is not covered by any lint or boot check. SHO-04/05/06 do not catch it. `OccluderPolygon2D.closed` defaults to true (probed).
    amendment: Add SHO-07 (E4 boot walk, and a content-validation rule): for every shadow-casting light anchor, the cell centre `p + CELL_CENTRE` must not lie inside any OCCLUDES_LIGHT box (the same doubled-box test as EM-20(b)); otherwise the light is demoted to non-shadow or the content fails validation. Record the polygon `closed` value as true in SHO-05.
  E4 [low] Snap-flag evidence is narrower than the rule built on it. P-5 and P-11 show a `SubViewport`'s snap flags do not round a `Light2D` position, but ADR-0008 (line 132) also makes the project settings `rendering/2d/snap/snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel` and `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel` required true, and says snapping rounds to nearest in base-pixel space. The probe set only the SubViewport flags in a minimal scene. If a path (the root viewport, a CanvasLayer, a different engine patch) snaps a light, 100.5 rounds to 101 and the lattice identity silently becomes an integer node, which P-7 and P-8 show is worse. SHO-03 checks node `global_position` and cannot see a renderer-side snap.
    amendment: SO-P5 must run with both the project settings and the SubViewport flags as ADR-0008 ships them, in the shipped scene tree (PipelineRoot wiring), and the drawn-lit comparison, not `global_position`, is the assertion. State in ADR-0008 that snapping applies to CanvasItem draw transforms and was probed not to apply to Light2D positions.
  E5 [low] Engine gotchas not stated: (a) `LightOccluder2D.sdf_collision` defaults to true (probed), which makes pooled occluders SDF contributors; set false unless something samples the SDF (cost UNVERIFIED). (b) `Light2D.shadow_item_cull_mask` and `LightOccluder2D.occluder_light_mask` both default to 1; the occluder builder and every shadow-casting light should set them explicitly so a later layer change cannot silently drop shadows. (c) `Light2D.shadow_filter_smooth` exists alongside `shadow_filter`, and SO-P8 only varies the enum, so PCF results are incomplete. (d) shadow resolution is bounded by `rendering/2d/shadow_atlas/size`, shared across shadow lights; the ADR names `SHADOW_ATLAS_PX` but SO-P6 does not require recording it.
    amendment: Add to § 3.3 / SHO-05: occluder pool nodes set `sdf_collision = false`, `occluder_light_mask` and the light's `shadow_item_cull_mask` explicitly. Extend SO-P8 to record `shadow_filter_smooth` and the atlas size with each count.
  E6 [info] Verified headless on 4.7.2 (no finding against the ADR): `const CELL_CENTRE: Vector2 = Vector2(0.5, 0.5)` compiles (a builtin value type, not a constructed Object); `static func` bodies of Placement.put_light_origin, BeamOffset.offset_for and ShadowOrigin.render_origin compile and run; `enum Mode {..}` is fine; `Vector2(Vector2i)` is exact; `x + 0.5` is exactly representable in float32 at 8388607 (so the 2^23 bound and WORLD_COORD_LIMIT 4194304 = 2^22 with a factor of two to spare are correct); `OccluderPolygon2D.CULL_DISABLED/CLOCKWISE/COUNTER_CLOCKWISE` and `Light2D.SHADOW_FILTER_NONE/PCF5/PCF13` exist with the names used; `SubViewport.size_2d_override_stretch`, `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel` and `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel` exist (defaults false). The PackedByteArray parameters of `mismatches_at_radius` are read-only, so by-reference passing and the 4.7 element-write change do not matter. There are no overrides, so the typed-return rule is not triggered, and no parameter is named get/set/free/call. Display note: `print(Vector2)` rounds large values (8388607.5 prints as 8388608); use `%.1f` or `is_equal_approx` in test output.
    amendment: None required. Keep test assertions on exact float equality, not on printed text.
  
  ADR-0018 review verdict CONCERNS. The decision itself is sound and the spike gating is stated honestly. The problem statement is clear, with the parallax arithmetic and the two frame facts. The eight alternatives were genuinely weighed. The negative consequences are stated, including the two-origin model, the fractional-position exception and the single-machine evidence. The engine is stamped as Godot 4.7.2, and the domain is marked HIGH risk with every engine claim probed or UNVERIFIED. TR-light-015 is decided here, and the owned-elsewhere rows are mapped. Three things must be amended before Accept, but none needs a rewrite. First, the lattice exception contradicts three registry stances and two live TR rows, and nothing syncs them. Second, the boot combination invariant in section 6 depends on an Emitter tuning row that the now-written ADR-0017 does not have, and the check is vacuous at ship. Third, no one owns the beam Light2D's parent across BODY_TRANSFER, and the identity contract fails on a pod hop or a weld rebase. The non-blocking items cover sibling wording, an evidence gap in the probes that support rung B, and right-sizing.:
  T1 [HIGH, BLOCKING] The CELL_CENTRE lattice rule (§ 3.1) and the offset writer (§ 4.2) contradict binding registry stances and live TR rows, and the ADR syncs neither. docs/registry/architecture.yaml line 961 says presentation coordinates are integer-valued float32, converted from Vector2i only at Placement.put and the canvas_transform write; put_light_origin adds a third conversion site that writes a non-integer value. Line 971 (sim_motion_interpolation) says positions are written only through Placement.put or put_control. Line 1398, the forbidden pattern, says the position, global position, offset and transform of any Node2D are written only in placement.gd and the named allow-list. Light2D is a Node2D, so beam_offset_writer.gd breaks this rule directly; F2's note 'distinct from Sprite2D.offset' does not exempt it. TR-pxl-005 (every node at integer base px, 'incl. the beam chest point', PR-4 rule 2) and TR-pc-026 (Light2D position by a 'floored lerp with zero fractional part') are contradicted too. Yet the 'GDD syncs this ADR requests' list in § Related names only the lighting and emitter GDDs. An Accepted ADR would then contradict three registry rows and two TR rows.
    amendment: Extend F1 and F2 to name registry rows 961, 971 and 1398 and request their amendment together with the ADR-0009 § 4 and ADR-0010 § 6.6 changes. Row 961 gains put_light_origin as a conversion site for Light2D lattice positions. Row 971 notes that a Light2D position is Placement.at plus CELL_CENTRE through put_light_origin. Row 1398's allow-list gains placement.gd put_light_origin (Light2D position) and lighting/beam_offset_writer.gd (Light2D offset). Add two entries to § Related's GDD sync list: pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md PR-4 rule 2, and the player-controller-input.md rule behind TR-pc-026. Both should read 'Light2D position is the floored cell plus CELL_CENTRE'. Re-word the TR-pxl-005 and TR-pc-026 rows to match. Make Acceptance of ADR-0018 conditional on ADR-0009 accepting F1 (OQ-A), as Validation already implies.
  T2 [MEDIUM, BLOCKING] Section 6's boot invariant LIGHT_SHADOW_ORIGIN_COMBO checks the pair (Emitter OCC_ORIGIN_MODE, SHADOW_ORIGIN_MODE). It assumes 'OCC_ORIGIN_MODE is reserved in ADR-0017's tuning with one value (FOOT)'. ADR-0017 is now on disk and has no OCC_ORIGIN_MODE row and no occ_origin field. Its D5.3 implements the foot origin as the function EmitterDerived.occlusion_origin, and D5.3/R8 say the spike changes that function 'and nothing else'. At ship the only reachable pairs are (FOOT, 0) and (FOOT, 1), both legal, so the invariant can never fire. It still costs a cross-module data row, a domain-2 boot code reserved through F3, test SHO-T5 and the 2x3 matrix. Separately, the Last Verified line still says ADR-0017 is not yet on disk.
    amendment: Remove the Emitter-side OCC_ORIGIN_MODE reservation, the LIGHT_SHADOW_ORIGIN_COMBO invariant, its F3 boot-code reservation and SHO-T5 from the present decision. SHADOW_ORIGIN_MODE keeps values {0 FOOT_OFFSET, 1 CHEST_NODE}. State in § 7 that the outcome-D amendment adds value 2, the Emitter mode row and the combination invariant together, so the check exists only when it can fail. Re-verify every ADR-0017 statement in Cross-ADR Assumptions and Last Verified against the ADR-0017 text now on disk, for example 'occ_origin' as computed by occlusion_origin(row, out_xy) and not a stored beam_pose field. The registry beam_pose expression (entities.yaml 4274, occ_origin = pos_curr) already backs the semantics.
  T3 [HIGH, BLOCKING] Section 4.1 makes the beam PointLight2D 'a child of a non-rotating body-frame node (never of the avatar)'. The Presenter writes its position as the actor's foot in the frame of body_of_actor. Nothing says which node that parent is, or who reparents the light when the actor's body changes. ADR-0034 § 8 reparents only the Presenter node on BODY_TRANSFER, in stage 0. ADR-0034's assumptions leave Lighting's pooled nodes outside BodyScenes 'unless it chooses to'. On a pod hop, or when the parent root is wrong for any frame, the light is placed in the wrong frame and O_draw differs from render(O_sim) by the inter-body canvas offset. That is the P1 drawn-against-simulated lie that SO-1 exists to prevent. SHO-03 checks only the fractional lattice, so it cannot catch a wrong-root error. SHO-04 checks only that the parent does not rotate.
    amendment: Add to § 4.1: 'The beam Light2D's parent is the translation-only BodyRoot of BodyView.body_of_actor(actor). It is attached through BodyScenes, so the stage-0 BODY_TRANSFER reparent moves it in the same frame as the Presenter node, before the stage-2 position write.' Extend SHO-04 to assert parent == BodyRoot(body_of_actor(actor)) every dev frame, with a new counter shadow_origin_wrong_frame. Add one SHO-T6 fixture covering a pod hop and a weld rebase with zero wrong-frame frames. The cross-ADR owner of the attach path is ADR-0034.
  T4 [MEDIUM] The evidence cited for rung B ('the 2026-10-29 probes already support B', P-9 '0 mismatches at every s') does not exercise a light quad that excludes the foot. By the ADR's own text, every probe used a 1200x1200 texture in a 400x300 viewport, and P-9 used a full-circle light. The 'Not probed' list names both 'a textured cone with the real edge-apex layout' and 'occluder culling by the light's range'. Under B with an edge-apex cone (LO-15), the quad starts at the chest and points along the aim. A wall lying wholly between the foot and the apex, for example AC-57 s = 1 aiming north, can sit outside the quad. OQ-E and § 4.4 frame engine-side culling as a question of how large OCC_MARGIN_PX must be. But OCC_MARGIN_PX sizes Lighting's own occluder set and cannot change what the engine culls, so if the engine culls by quad extent the question is a pass condition for B. The ladder also has no texture-side B variant, so such a failure would fall through A, which is predicted to fail, to D, a Core simulation change. How the engine culls is UNVERIFIED and is not asserted here.
    amendment: Reframe OQ-E as a B pass condition rather than margin sizing. Add one row to the § 8.2 probe pack, SO-P10. It uses the real edge-apex beam texture at its shipped size, with a wall wholly between foot and apex and the aim pointing away from the foot, at AC-57 s = 1 and s = 10, plus a far-reach case with a large offset. Its pass condition is zero radius-2 mismatches. Add a rung B-pad between B and A: same node and offset, but the beam texture (or texture_scale plus transparent padding) is sized so the quad contains the foot cell, with the fill-rate cost measured in spike step 3. State that D is reached only if B-pad also fails.
  T5 [LOW] Right-sizing of the lint pack. SHO-05 (cull mode) and SHO-06 (integer vertices, plus vertex-set equality with the OCCLUDES_LIGHT rectangles) restate the occluder builder's own LO-11 set-equality contract. ADR-0014 and ADR-0028 own that builder (TR-light-014 and TR-light-035 are listed here as owned elsewhere). Keeping both here creates two homes for one test.
    amendment: Keep SHO-01 to SHO-04 in this ADR. Move SHO-05 and SHO-06 into ADR-0028's occluder-builder tests as item (c) of the § 1 fold-down list, keeping only the constraints here: CULL_DISABLED, integer vertices, no shift.
  T6 [LOW] Right-sizing of the spike matrix. § 8.1 multiplies configurations: 2 reference machines, 2 renderers, the shipped filter plus NONE, and pass A plus possibly pass B. Each configuration runs SO-P7's 140 rows with retained captures named per s and aim. For a solo or small-team Sprint-0 story that is roughly 1,000 to 2,000 rows of evidence. Most of it tells the same thing once B passes on the pinned configuration.
    amendment: Run the full 140-row SO-P7 matrix on the pinned configuration: Forward+ on Vulkan, template_release, shipped shadow_filter, pass A, on both RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK. On every other configuration (Compatibility, the NONE filter, pass B) run a reduced subset: s in {1, 20, 34}, 4 aims, and the idle and run CHEST_POINT rows. Escalate to the full matrix only when a subset row fails. State that the escalation is part of the selection rule in § 5.
  
  CROSS-ADR RULINGS (binding):
  CT-24 owner ADR-0015 (align: ADR-0017, ADR-0018, ADR-0013, ADR-0034): Merges the 0015-review coordinate-bound item and the 0017-review BODY_COORD_LIMIT item. ADR-0017 I-BOUNDS cites a BODY_COORD_LIMIT that ADR-0015 never defines. ADR-0018 assumes foot + 0.5 is exact in float32, but a canvas coordinate can reach 2^23, and at that magnitude x + 0.5 is not exact.
    amendment: ADR-0015 adds BODY_COORD_LIMIT (BodyTuning plus the bounds ledger, at most 2^24, derived from max section extent times max sections per body). It is restore-checked and must be repeated by Layout in `can_attach`. ADR-0015 also publishes the canvas bound: `|world_a - world_b| + |pos| < 2^23` holds under WEB_COORD_BUDGET_PX, and otherwise WORLD_COORD_LIMIT is lowered. ADR-0017 (I-BOUNDS and the section 11 int32 column-sufficiency statement), ADR-0018 (the 0.5-lattice assumption) and ADR-0034 cite these two numbers. ADR-0013 `can_attach` adds the BODY_COORD_LIMIT check.
  CT-29 owner ADR-0019 (align: ADR-0018, ADR-0009): Merges the 0019-review Light2D item, 0018-review items 2 and 7, and ADR-0019 T2. ADR-0018 owns the shadow-origin rule (mode B): the beam Light2D sits at the foot cell plus CELL_CENTRE, written through `Placement.put_light_origin`, and the chest is the cone apex only. ADR-0019 adopts this verbatim. To avoid a Depends On cycle (ADR-0019 -> 0018 -> 0017 -> 0019), ADR-0019 cites ADR-0018 under Related and Blocked stories, not Depends On, which matches ADR-0018's existing Blocks row.
    amendment: ADR-0019 section 7.1: the beam Light2D is excepted from the 'every written position has a zero fractional part' statement, and the chest offset is read from ControllerView for the apex and offset terms only. Section 7.2 allow-list entry: 'the beam Light2D's position through `Placement.put_light_origin` at the interpolated foot cell from body.state plus CELL_CENTRE under ADR-0018 SHADOW_ORIGIN_MODE 0 (the chest cell under 1), and its rotation, which may be fractional; the sprite position uses `Placement.put`; the beam node's `offset` is not a Presenter write (ADR-0018 `beam_offset_writer.gd`)'. CTL-11's allow-list adds `put_light_origin`, and CTL-11 and PRES-03 point at ADR-0018's allow-list entry. Add ADR-0018 to Related. ADR-0009 F1 supplies `put_light_origin` (foundation_amendments).
  CT-30 owner ADR-0018 (align: ADR-0017): Merges 0018-review items 1 and 8 and ADR-0018 T2. ADR-0017 is on disk. It has neither `beam_pose.occ_origin` nor OCC_ORIGIN_MODE; it has the function `EmitterDerived.occlusion_origin`. At ship the only reachable pairs are legal, so the combination invariant can never fire. It is removed now and comes back with outcome D. ADR-0017 only widens its contingency wording. The 0017-review alternative, adding `occ_origin_x_of` and OCC_ORIGIN_MODE now, is rejected.
    amendment: ADR-0018: remove the Emitter-side OCC_ORIGIN_MODE reservation, LIGHT_SHADOW_ORIGIN_COMBO, its F3 boot-code reservation and SHO-T5. SHADOW_ORIGIN_MODE keeps {0 FOOT_OFFSET, 1 CHEST_NODE}. Section 7 states that the outcome-D amendment adds value 2, the Emitter mode row and the combination invariant together. Rename `occ_origin` to `occlusion_origin` throughout, as computed by `EmitterDerived.occlusion_origin(row, out_xy)`. Re-verify every ADR-0017 statement in Cross-ADR Assumptions and Last Verified against the ADR-0017 text on disk, and delete 'not yet on disk'. ADR-0017 D5.3, R8 and the open-question list: 'outcome D replaces `occlusion_origin` and adds a hot, allocation-free EmitterView read of the beam's previous and current occlusion origin (two int pairs, derived each tick) and the OCC_ORIGIN_MODE tuning row, introduced together with ADR-0018's combination invariant; no change while B or A ships'.
  CT-31 owner ADR-0018 (align: ADR-0014, ADR-0028): Merges 0014-review item 4 and ADR-0014 T2. ADR-0018 assumes half-open output, but ADR-0014 returns occupied spans, and ADR-0017 D8.2 already reads them correctly. Built as ADR-0018 is worded, the polygons would be 1 px smaller than the boxes the Emitter tests.
    amendment: ADR-0018 Related (line 413): '`rects_in`/`section_rects_into` return OCCLUDES_LIGHT occupied spans (x0, y0, x1-1, y1-1) in the body frame. Polygon corners are (x0, y0) and (x1_occ+1, y1_occ+1). Layout applies no shift. This is the convention of ADR-0017 D8.2.' ADR-0014 replaces 'ADR-0018: No constraint' with: 'ADR-0018 and ADR-0028 read `spans` as occupied spans; a polygon corner is at (x0, y0) and (x1_occ + 1, y1_occ + 1); Layout applies no shift.' ADR-0028 inherits this wording when it is written.
  CT-32 owner ADR-0034 (align: ADR-0018, ADR-0019, ADR-0015, ADR-0023, ADR-0028): Merges the 0019-review attach_presenter item, 0018-review item 6 and ADR-0018 T3, 0015-review item 2 (V8 reparent) and the 0034-review Horror rebind item. ADR-0034 owns BodyScenes and the stage-0 BODY_TRANSFER pass. The beam light's frame is currently unowned. Probe: `reparent` preserves the global transform by default. Ruling: use `reparent(p, false)`. The node's owning presenter rewrites its position from the new frame in the same frame, before draw (stage AVATAR 2 or LIGHTING 6 runs after stage 0). The projector writes no foreign node's position.
    amendment: ADR-0034 section 8: BodyScenes namespaces gain LIGHTING, for the beam and actor-following Light2D nodes, keyed by the seat's beam id. On BODY_TRANSFER, stage 0 reparents the Presenter node and every LIGHTING node of that actor in one pass, before stage AVATAR (2), to the translation-only BodyRoot of `BodyView.body_of_actor(actor)`, through `SceneMove` `reparent(p, false)`. The owning presenter writes the position from `BodyView.pos_x/pos_y` in the same frame. A dev assertion checks that every reparented node received an owner position write before draw. Add `BodyScenes.rebind(node, body_id, section_id)` and state the caller's duty to call it when its owner's section changes (an assumption on ADR-0023's Horror rigs). ADR-0015 marks V8 'answered by probe 2026-10-29, keep_global_transform false, owner rewrites position'. ADR-0018 section 4.1: 'The beam Light2D's parent is the translation-only BodyRoot of `body_of_actor(actor)`, attached through BodyScenes LIGHTING, so the stage-0 BODY_TRANSFER reparent moves it before the stage-2 write.' Extend SHO-04 to assert `parent == BodyRoot(body_of_actor(actor))` on every dev frame (counter `shadow_origin_wrong_frame`), and add SHO-T6 (pod hop and weld rebase, zero wrong-frame frames). ADR-0019 section 7.1 adds one sentence adopting `attach_presenter` and the stage-0 reparent.
  CT-54 owner ADR-0010 (align: ADR-0011, ADR-0012, ADR-0013, ADR-0014, ADR-0015, ADR-0016, ADR-0017, ADR-0018, ADR-0019): Merges every ADR-0010 ask: accessor naming, SIM-04, `static var` (0011-review); UNUSED_PARAMETER on `@abstract` and `@abstract` placement (0013-review, 0014-review, 0015-review); HOT-01 Layout tags (0013-review); can_instantiate for static-only classes (0012-review); the CNT-03 QueryBuffer exemption, the placeholder signature and READ-03 (0014-review); `bind`, SIM-06 and SIM-09 (0015-review); dictionary_variant (0016-review); PRES-03 Light2D (0018-review); field_writers globs (CT-07). The changes are listed in foundation_amendments. The Core ADRs only align: ADR-0011 keeps bare accessor names (legal once the rule is reworded) and ADR-0019 keeps `get_` names. Each view uses one style throughout.
    amendment: No Core text beyond the alignments named in CT-07, CT-19 and CT-29. ADR-0013 E9 wording cites ADR-0010 section 6.6 HOT-01 for the Layout Tier H tag list. ADR-0014's Acceptance stays conditional on the CNT-03 exemption landing.

attachment.content:
- adopt: Brownfield audit — do existing artifacts actually work? Numbered migration plan. Unlike /project-stage-detect, checks compliance not existence.
- agents-sdk: Build, debug, or review Cloudflare Agents SDK applications using the agents package.
- architecture-decision: Create an ADR documenting a technical decision: context, alternatives considered, consequences.
- architecture-review: Traceability matrix mapping GDD requirements to ADRs. Finds gaps, cross-ADR conflicts, engine compatibility. PASS/CONCERNS/NOT ASSESSED/FAIL.
- art-bible: Author the Art Bible — visual identity gating asset production. Run before /map-systems.
- asset-audit: Audit assets against naming conventions, file size budgets, format standards. Finds orphaned assets, missing references.
- asset-spec: Per-asset visual specs plus AI generation prompts from GDDs and character profiles. After the art bible.
- balance-check: Find balance outliers, broken progressions, degenerate strategies, economy imbalances in formulas and data. 'Check game balance'.
- basin: Build and troubleshoot Cloudflare Basin analytics workflows with Basin Pipelines, Basin Catalog, and Basin SQL. Use for streaming data into R2 Iceberg tables, managing catalogs, or querying those tables; also use for requests using the former Data Platform, Pipelines, R2 Data Catalog, or R2 SQL names.
- brainstorm: Guided concept ideation using professional studio techniques, player psychology, creative exploration.
- brownfield: First-principles audit and improvement plan for an EXISTING codebase ("brownfield" project) — especially one the user can run and demo but can't confidently judge. Orchestrates parallel specialist subagents (architecture, product-intent, code, tests, security, performance, docs) that treat existing code as evidence rather than ground truth, keeps an assumptions register and escalates the risky ones, writes a consolidated improvement design doc with a dependency-ordered PR plan sized to the repo, runs a writer↔reviewer loop until no critical/major issues remain, and optionally (--execute) implements the plan as worktree-isolated, reviewed git branches. Use this skill whenever the user says /brownfield, asks to audit / health-check / assess / sanity-check / "second opinion" an existing repo or legacy app, asks "is this built correctly?", "what's wrong with this codebase?", "a contractor/AI built this and I'm not sure it's right", wants a prioritized improvement or remediation plan for code that already exists, or is inheriting a project and wants to know where the bodies are buried — even if they never use the word "brownfield". Not for greenfield design of new systems or for reviewing a single small diff/PR.
- bug-report: Structured bug report from a description, or analyze code for potential bugs. Reproduction steps, severity.
- bug-triage: Re-evaluate open bugs — priority vs severity, assign to sprints, surface systemic trends. Run when the count grows.
- ccgs-code-review: Architectural code review — coding standards, SOLID, testability, performance concerns.
- changelog: Auto-generate a changelog from git commits and sprint data. Internal and player-facing versions.
- cloudflare: Discover and choose Cloudflare products for apps, APIs, AI agents, storage, networking, and security. Use for architecture and product selection, including when the user describes a need without naming a Cloudflare product; then find the relevant skill or documentation.
- cloudflare-email-service: Implement or troubleshoot Cloudflare Email Sending and Email Routing integrations and their delivery configuration.
- cloudflare-one: Design, configure, troubleshoot, or review Cloudflare One Zero Trust and SASE deployments. Use cloudflare-one-migrations for migration planning from other vendors.
- cloudflare-one-migrations: Assess and plan migrations from existing VPN, SWG, or SASE platforms to Cloudflare One, including policy mapping, parity gaps, and rollout.
- code-review: Review a branch, PR, commit range, or working tree with separate Standards and Spec tasks through review_run. Use when the user asks for a code review or asks to review changes since a fixed point.
- consistency-check: Scan GDDs against the entity registry for cross-document conflicts. Grep-first approach targets conflicting sections, different stats.
- content-audit: Audit GDD content counts against what's implemented — planned vs built.
- create-architecture: Author the architecture blueprint before code is written. Validates decisions against the pinned engine, flags knowledge gaps.
- create-control-manifest: Flat must-do/never-do rules sheet per system and layer, extracted from Accepted ADRs. ADRs explain why; this is actionable.
- create-epics: Turn GDDs plus architecture into epics — one per architectural module, with untraced requirements. Then /create-stories [epic-slug].
- create-stories: Break one epic into implementable stories embedding TR-ID, ADR guidance, acceptance criteria. Reads the control manifest. After /create-epics.
- design-review: Reviews one design document for completeness, internal consistency, implementability, and design standards. Before handing to programmers.
- design-system: Section-by-section GDD authoring for one system — walks through each required section, cross-references dependencies.
- durable-objects: Build, debug, or review Cloudflare Durable Objects code for persistent state and coordination.
- estimate: Estimate task effort from complexity, dependencies, velocity, risk. Structured estimate with confidence levels.
- gate-check: Ready to advance between development phases? PASS/CONCERNS/NOT ASSESSED/FAIL with blockers and required artifacts. 'Can we move to production?'
- help: What should I do next? Use when stuck or you don't know what to do.
- k2: Build and troubleshoot Cloudflare K2 or K2 Streams durable logs. Use for stream setup, producing from Workers or HTTP, configuring retention and inputs, and consuming through subscriptions.
- launch-checklist: Launch readiness across every department: code, content, store, marketing, community, infrastructure, legal, go/no-go sign-offs.
- legion: Route legion <command> requests to the Legion CLI for Claude Code.
- localize: Localization pipeline — find hardcoded strings, extract string tables, cultural review, VO, RTL, enforce string freeze.
- map-systems: Decompose a concept into individual systems, map dependencies, prioritize design order, create the systems index.
- milestone-review: Milestone progress review — completeness, quality metrics, risk, go/no-go recommendation. At checkpoints or before a deadline.
- nextjs-on-cloudflare: Build, migrate, and deploy Next.js apps on Cloudflare Workers with vinext. Use when starting a Next.js project on Cloudflare, moving an existing app to Workers, choosing between vinext and OpenNext, or setting up vinext for Workers. For setup, migration, or deployment, install vinext's upstream skills with `npx skills add cloudflare/vinext` if missing, then read and follow the applicable skill and docs.
- onboard: Onboarding doc for a new contributor or agent — project state, conventions, priorities relevant to the specified role.
- orchestrate-omp: Coordinate OMP subagents on substantial work. Use when parallel discovery, specialist review, or clearly partitioned implementation will shorten or strengthen the result; skip trivial tasks.
- patch-notes: Player-facing patch notes from git history and changelogs. Translates developer language into player communication.
- perf-profile: Performance profiling — find bottlenecks, measure against budgets, produce ranked optimization recommendations.
- playtest-report: Structured playtest report template, or turn existing playtest notes into structured feedback.
- project-stage-detect: Analyze project state, detect stage, identify gaps, recommend next steps. 'Where are we in development?'
- propagate-design-change: A GDD changed — scan ADRs and the traceability index for now-stale architectural decisions. Impact report, guides resolution.
- prototype: Concept prototype before GDDs — throwaway HTML, Engine or Paper build, PROCEED/PIVOT/KILL/NOT ASSESSED. After /brainstorm and /setup-engine.
- pstack-omp: OMP adapter for poteto-mode. Maps canonical pstack roles and lifecycle protocols to current OMP task agents, batching, isolation, IRC follow-ups, and durable result resources.
- qa-plan: QA test plan for a sprint — classifies stories by Logic/Integration/Visual/UI, covers automated tests, manual cases, smoke scope.
- quick-design: Lightweight spec for small changes — tuning adjustments, minor mechanics. Embeds directly into stories; skips full GDD.
- regression-suite: Map test coverage to GDD critical paths, find fixed bugs lacking regression tests, flag drift from new features.
- release-checklist: Pre-release checklist — build verification, certification requirements, store metadata, launch readiness.
- research: Research a question with high-trust primary sources and save cited findings. Use when the user requests research, documentation facts, or API facts.
- retrospective: Sprint or milestone retrospective from completed work, velocity, blockers. Actionable insights for the next iteration.
- reverse-document: Generate missing design or architecture docs from existing implementation — works backwards from code and prototypes.
- review-all-gdds: Holistic cross-GDD review — contradictions between systems, dominant strategies, economic imbalance, cognitive overload, pillar drift.
- sandbox-migrate-to-next: Migrate Cloudflare Sandbox apps from stable @cloudflare/sandbox to @cloudflare/sandbox@next (SDK 1.0 preview). Use sandbox-next for apps already on the preview.
- sandbox-next: Build or maintain Cloudflare Sandbox apps on @cloudflare/sandbox@next (SDK 1.0 preview). Use sandbox-migrate-to-next when porting a stable app.
- sandbox-stable: Build or maintain Cloudflare Sandbox apps on the stable @cloudflare/sandbox package. Use sandbox-next for preview apps and sandbox-migrate-to-next for stable-to-preview migrations.
- scope-check: Scope creep check — current scope versus the original plan. Flags additions, quantifies bloat, recommends cuts. 'Any scope creep?'
- security-audit: Security audit — save tampering, cheat vectors, network exploits, data exposure, input validation. Before public or multiplayer release.
- settings: View or change project config — effective merged values, or set locally in project.local.yaml.
- setup-engine: Configure engine and version. Pins it in CLAUDE.md; WebSearch fills reference docs when the version is beyond LLM training data.
- skill-improve: Improve a skill via a test-fix-retest loop — static checks, targeted fixes, keep or revert on score change.

- soak-test: Soak test protocol for extended play — what to observe and log for slow leaks, fatigue, late-appearing edge cases.
- sprint-plan: New or updated sprint plan from the current milestone, completed work, and available capacity.

- start: First-time onboarding — asks where you are, then guides you to the right workflow.

# Global instructions (all projects)

## Dynamic Workflows: model choice

- Always use Sonnet 5.5 (`model: 'sonnet'`) or Haiku (`model: 'haiku'`) for worker agents in Dynamic Workflows (the Workflow tool's `agent()` calls), to preserve token usage. Use Haiku for mechanical stages (logging, formatting, simple extraction) and Sonnet for the rest.
- Opus or Fable is acceptable only as an advisor where needed: a senior reviewer, judge or verdict seat, never for bulk work such as planners, writers, fixers or scanners.
- Set `model` explicitly on every worker `agent()` call; do not let workers inherit the session model.

# Claude Code Game Studios -- Game Studio Agent Architecture

Indie game development managed through 49 coordinated Claude Code subagents.
Each agent owns a specific domain, enforcing separation of concerns and quality.

## Technology Stack

- **Engine**: Godot 4.7.2
- **Language**: GDScript
- **Version Control**: Git with trunk-based development
- **Build System**: SCons (engine), Godot Export Templates
- **Asset Pipeline**: Godot Import System + custom resource pipeline

> **Note**: Engine-specialist agents exist for Godot, Unity, and Unreal with
> dedicated sub-specialists. Use the set matching your engine.

## Project Structure

@.claude/docs/directory-structure.md

## Engine Version Reference

@docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md


## Technical Preferences

`project.yaml` at the repo root is the primary config store — engine, specialists,
naming, platform, performance, modes. Skills resolve it via `resolve_config`
(see `.claude/docs/config-resolution.md`).

`.claude/docs/technical-preferences.md` is the **legacy fallback**, read on demand
when a key is absent from `project.yaml`. It is not imported here: before
`/setup-engine` runs it is almost entirely `[TO BE CONFIGURED]` placeholders, and
after it runs `project.yaml` holds the real values.

## Coordination Rules

@.claude/docs/coordination-rules.md

## Collaboration Protocol

**User-driven collaboration, not autonomous execution.**
Every task follows: **Question -> Options -> Decision -> Draft -> Approval**

- Agents MUST ask "May I write this to [filepath]?" before using Write/Edit tools
  (exempt: `active.md` appends, agent memory, a subagent's new file at the path
  its orchestrating skill named; see `.claude/rules/agent-memory.md`)
- Agents MUST show drafts or summaries before requesting approval
- Multi-file changes require explicit approval for the full changeset
- No commits without user instruction
- A skipped or dismissed question is not an answer: act on nothing, re-ask in
  plain text and wait
- Started outside this file's folder? Warn first: hooks, deny rules and the
  ask-first mode load only when Claude Code starts here

See `docs/COLLABORATIVE-DESIGN-PRINCIPLE.md` for full protocol and examples.

> **First session?** If the project has no engine configured and no game concept,
> run `/start` to begin the guided onboarding flow.

## Coding Standards

@.claude/docs/coding-standards.md

## Context Management

Read `.claude/docs/context-management.md` on demand — it is a reference, not
session context. Two of its conventions are load-bearing and cited by name
elsewhere in the repo, so they are restated here rather than lost:

- **`production/session-state/active.md` is the session checkpoint.** The file is
  the memory, not the conversation. Read it first after any compaction, crash, or
  `/clear`.
- **Helpers in `.claude/scripts/` emit observations, never verdicts.** A script
  that scores or judges will eventually contradict a mode or override it cannot
  see. (Cited by `artifact-check.sh` and `adr-dep-graph.sh`.)

# Directory Structure

```text
/
├── CLAUDE.md                    # Master configuration
├── project.yaml                 # Machine-readable project config — engine, modes, stage (source of truth)
├── .claude/                     # Agent definitions, skills, hooks, rules, docs
├── <code root>/                 # Game source code — THE PATH IS ENGINE-SPECIFIC, see below
├── assets/                      # Game assets (art, audio, vfx, shaders, data)
├── design/                      # Game design documents (gdd, narrative, levels, balance)
├── docs/                        # Technical documentation (architecture, api, postmortems)
│   └── engine-reference/        # Curated engine API snapshots (version-pinned)
├── tests/                       # Game test suites (unit, integration, performance, playtest)
├── tools/                       # Build and pipeline tools (ci, build, asset-pipeline)
├── prototypes/                  # Throwaway prototypes (outside the code root)
├── production/                  # Production management (sprints, milestones, releases)
│   ├── session-state/           # Ephemeral session state (active.md — gitignored)
│   └── session-logs/            # Session audit trail (gitignored)
└── studio-tests/                # QA for the skills/agents themselves — /skill-test, /skill-improve
```

## The code root is engine-specific

**Two of the three supported engines will not build a project whose code sits in
`src/`.** This is not a style preference — it is a hard constraint of the engine's
own toolchain:

| `engine.name` | Code root | Why it cannot be `src/` |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `src/` | No constraint — Godot loads from `res://` anywhere under the project root. |
| **Unity** | `Assets/` | Unity compiles **only** `Assets/` and `Packages/`. Code outside them is invisible to the compiler. |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/` | UnrealBuildTool discovers modules under `Source/`; content lives in `Content/`. A module elsewhere is not built. |

**Resolve the code root from `engine.name` before writing any source file.** A
path shown as `src/…` alone is a Godot example: read it as *"the code root"* and
substitute the row above. `src/` is the table's Godot row, not a universal path.

**Tests follow the same rule** — the same compilers decide what they see:

| `engine.name` | Test root | Anywhere else |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `tests/unit/`, `tests/integration/` | — |
| **Unity** | `Assets/Tests/EditMode/`, `Assets/Tests/PlayMode/` | not compiled: "0 tests, Passed" |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/Private/Tests/` | not built: "No automation tests matched" |

Read `tests/unit/[system]/` (or `integration/`) anywhere as the test root plus `[System]/`.

# Godot Engine — Version Reference

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Engine Version** | Godot 4.7 |
| **Installed at pin time** | 4.7.2.stable.mono.official.ed1daf0bf (matches pin; probed 2026-10-25 at `C:/Users/dasbl/Documents/Godot/`). 4.6.2 standard is also installed, unused. |
| **Release Date** | June 2026 (latest patch: 4.7.2, August 2026) |
| **Project Pinned** | 2026-10-17 |
| **Last Docs Verified** | 2026-10-17 (release timeline and 4.7 changes); 2026-02-12 (4.4-4.6 content) |
| **LLM Knowledge Cutoff** | May 2025 |

## Knowledge Gap Warning

The LLM's training data likely covers Godot up to ~4.3. Versions 4.5, 4.6
and 4.7 were released after the cutoff and introduced significant changes that
the model does NOT know about; 4.4 came out shortly before it and may be thinly
covered. Always cross-reference this directory before suggesting Godot API calls.

## Installed-Version Gap Warning

The warning above is one-directional — it covers the **model** knowing less than
this pin. The reverse gap is real and `/setup-engine` §3 creates it deliberately
("pin the newer one and upgrade later"): this reference can sit **ahead of the
installed editor**, and an agent citing it correctly then emits APIs that do not
compile locally. **Check `Installed at pin time` above before trusting a
version-qualified claim** — `NOT DETERMINED` means the gap is unknown, not absent.

## Post-Cutoff Version Timeline

| Version | Release | Risk Level | Key Theme |
|---------|---------|------------|-----------|
| 4.5 | Sep 2025 | HIGH | Accessibility (AccessKit), variadic args, @abstract, shader baker, SMAA |
| 4.6 | Jan 2026 | HIGH | Jolt default, glow rework, D3D12 default on Windows, IK restored |
| 4.7 | Jun 2026 | HIGH | AreaLight3D, HDR output, Asset Store replaces the Asset Library, VirtualJoystick, Jolt soft-body and world-boundary changes, typed-return overrides |

## Before the Cutoff

4.4 (Mar 2025, Jolt option, FileAccess return types) predates the May 2025
cutoff; the Knowledge Gap Warning still applies to it.

Dates from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/releases, checked 2026-10-17:
4.4 Mar 3 2025, 4.5 Sep 15 2025, 4.6 Jan 26 2026, 4.7 Jun 18 2026, 4.7.2 Aug 18
2026. Migration guides and release notes: `breaking-changes.md` § Sources.

# Agent Coordination Rules

1. **Vertical Delegation**: Leadership agents delegate to department leads, who
   delegate to specialists. Never skip a tier for complex decisions.
2. **Horizontal Consultation**: Agents at the same tier may consult each other
   but must not make binding decisions outside their domain.
3. **Conflict Resolution**: When two agents disagree, escalate to the shared
   parent. If no shared parent, escalate to `creative-director` for design
   conflicts or `technical-director` for technical conflicts.
4. **Change Propagation**: When a design change affects multiple domains, the
   `producer` agent coordinates the propagation.
5. **No Unilateral Cross-Domain Changes**: An agent must never modify files
   outside its designated directories without explicit delegation.
6. **Read Design Docs by Section**: A brief names the sections an agent needs
   by heading. Find a heading in a GDD, ADR or the art bible with the Grep
   tool (`^#`, content mode) and Read that range with offset and limit; read a doc
   whole only when the task needs all of it, and say why. `validate-read.sh`
   refuses a whole-file read of a doc over 40 KB.
7. **Nothing Goes Upstream**: Never file, open or comment on an issue or pull
   request in an engine, plugin or vendor repository, even when asked. Write a
   draft (`/bug-report` drafts only) and the user submits it.

## Model Tier Assignment

Read `.claude/docs/model-tiers.md` on demand. It carries the tier table, the
per-skill assignments and the authoring rule.

**Key point:** whether a skill's `model:` is used
depends on how the skill starts. Typed as `/skill-name`: yes, except a `haiku`
pin in auto mode. Started by Claude through the Skill tool: no. Never tell a
user a `haiku` skill saves money; an `opus` skill typed in a Sonnet session
costs more. The agent-side `model:` is a different mechanism, and is applied.

## Subagents vs Agent Teams

This project uses two distinct multi-agent patterns:

### Subagents (current, always active)
Spawned via the `Agent` tool within a single Claude Code session. Used by all
`team-*` skills and orchestration skills. Subagents share the session's
permission context, run sequentially or in parallel within the session, and
return results to the parent.

**When to spawn in parallel**: If two subagents' inputs are independent (neither
needs the other's output to begin), spawn both `Agent` calls simultaneously
rather than waiting. Example: `/review-all-gdds` **Phase 2** (consistency) and
**Phase 3** (design theory) are independent — spawn both at the same time.
Phase 1 loads the GDDs and both depend on it, so it is the one phase here that
must NOT be parallelised.

### Agent Teams (experimental — opt-in)
Multiple independent Claude Code *sessions* coordinated via a shared task list.
Opt-in only — read `.claude/docs/agent-teams.md` on demand before proposing one.

## Parallel Task Protocol

When an orchestration skill spawns multiple independent agents:

1. Issue all independent `Agent` calls before waiting for any result
2. Collect all results before proceeding to dependent phases
3. If any agent is BLOCKED, surface it immediately — do not silently skip
4. Always produce a partial report if some agents complete and others block

# Coding Standards

- All game code must include doc comments on public APIs
- Architecture decisions are recorded as ADRs in `docs/architecture/`. **How many is
  set by `modes.workflow`** — all ADRs at `full`, *critical* ADRs only at `standard`,
  and none required at `minimal`, where the decision log and `design/game-brief.md`
  carry the rationale instead. See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.
- Gameplay values must be data-driven (external config), never hardcoded
- All public methods must be unit-testable (dependency injection over singletons)
- Commits must reference the relevant design document or task ID
- **Commit messages**: Use Conventional Commits format — `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`. Reference the story or task ID in the body (e.g., `Story: EPIC-001-S02`).
- **Verification-driven development**: Write tests first when adding gameplay systems.
  For UI changes, verify with screenshots. Compare expected output to actual output
  before marking work complete. Every implementation should have a way to prove it works.
- **A parse check is not a run.** Every story that changes something
  player-observable is launched and observed before it closes, and the
  observation is a retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/`. Procedure
  per engine: `.claude/docs/run-and-observe.md`. Not waived at
  `qa.level: minimal` — tests are, the look is not.

# Design Document Standards

- All design docs use Markdown
- Each mechanic has a dedicated document in `design/gdd/`
- **How many of the 8 sections are required depends on `modes.workflow`** —
  all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system defines numeric rules — rates,
  curves, thresholds, costs; the system's `Category` is a hint, not the test) at
  `standard`, and no
  GDD at all at `minimal`, where `design/game-brief.md` is the design record.
  See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`. The 8 sections:
  1. **Overview** -- one-paragraph summary
  2. **Player Fantasy** -- intended feeling and experience
  3. **Detailed Rules** -- unambiguous mechanics
  4. **Formulas** -- all math defined with variables
  5. **Edge Cases** -- unusual situations handled
  6. **Dependencies** -- other systems listed
  7. **Tuning Knobs** -- configurable values identified
  8. **Acceptance Criteria** -- testable success conditions
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale

# Testing Standards

## Test Evidence by Story Type

All stories must have appropriate test evidence before they can be marked Done:

| Story Type | Required Evidence | Location | Default Gate Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Logic** (formulas, AI, state machines) | Automated unit test — must pass | `tests/unit/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Integration** (multi-system) | Integration test OR documented playtest | `tests/integration/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Visual/Feel** (animation, VFX, feel) | Retained screenshot + lead sign-off | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **UI** (menus, HUD, screens) | Retained screenshot of each screen touched | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **Config/Data** (balance tuning) | Smoke check pass | `production/qa/smoke-[date].md` | ADVISORY |

The **Default Gate Level** applies when `testing.strict` is not set in
`project.yaml`. A project may override it per test type: `testing.strict.logic`,
`.integration`, `.visual`, `.ui`, and `.config` each take `true` (BLOCKING) or
`false` (ADVISORY). `/story-done`, `/story-readiness`, `/dev-story`,
`/gate-check`, and `/smoke-check` resolve the effective level from that setting,
falling back to the defaults above when it is absent.

> **Why Visual and UI block.** "Retained" is load-bearing — the screenshot must
> still be on disk in `production/qa/evidence/` when the story is closed. One
> that was captured and discarded is an assertion, not evidence. These two rows
> block because for a game the way it looks *is* the product: an advisory visual
> gate gets deferred in favour of whatever does block, and the result is a
> well-tested game that looks wrong.

> **Exception — `/smoke-check`.** The ADVISORY default for **Config/Data** above
> applies to *per-story evidence* gates. `/smoke-check` is a build-health gate,
> not a per-story evidence gate, so its own unset default for
> `testing.strict.config` is **BLOCKING**. The two defaults differ on purpose.

## Automated Test Rules

- **Naming**: per engine — `.claude/rules/test-standards.md`
- **Determinism**: Tests must produce the same result every run — no random seeds, no time-dependent assertions
- **Isolation**: Each test sets up and tears down its own state; tests must not depend on execution order
- **No hardcoded data**: Test fixtures use constant files or factory functions, not inline magic numbers
  (exception: boundary value tests where the exact number IS the point)
- **Independence**: Unit tests do not call external APIs, databases, or file I/O — use dependency injection

## What NOT to Automate

- Visual fidelity (shader output, VFX appearance, animation curves)
- "Feel" qualities (input responsiveness, perceived weight, timing)
- Platform-specific rendering (test on target hardware, not headlessly)
- Full gameplay sessions (covered by playtesting, not automation)

## CI/CD Rules

- Automated test suite runs on every push to main and every PR
- No merge if tests fail — tests are a blocking gate in CI
- Never disable or skip failing tests to make CI pass — fix the underlying issue
- Engine-specific CI commands:
  - **Godot**: `godot --headless -s -d --remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:0 res://addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd -a res://tests --ignoreHeadlessMode`
  - **Unity**: `game-ci/unity-test-runner@v4` (GitHub Actions)
  - **Unreal**: headless runner with `-nullrhi` flag
- [Consistency-check needs a confirming run](consistency-check-confirming-run.md) — owner+registry fixes leave leftovers in consumer GDDs; grep referenced_by docs, print patch counts

# Directory Structure

```text
/
├── CLAUDE.md                    # Master configuration
├── project.yaml                 # Machine-readable project config — engine, modes, stage (source of truth)
├── .claude/                     # Agent definitions, skills, hooks, rules, docs
├── <code root>/                 # Game source code — THE PATH IS ENGINE-SPECIFIC, see below
├── assets/                      # Game assets (art, audio, vfx, shaders, data)
├── design/                      # Game design documents (gdd, narrative, levels, balance)
├── docs/                        # Technical documentation (architecture, api, postmortems)
│   └── engine-reference/        # Curated engine API snapshots (version-pinned)
├── tests/                       # Game test suites (unit, integration, performance, playtest)
├── tools/                       # Build and pipeline tools (ci, build, asset-pipeline)
├── prototypes/                  # Throwaway prototypes (outside the code root)
├── production/                  # Production management (sprints, milestones, releases)
│   ├── session-state/           # Ephemeral session state (active.md — gitignored)
│   └── session-logs/            # Session audit trail (gitignored)
└── studio-tests/                # QA for the skills/agents themselves — /skill-test, /skill-improve
```

## The code root is engine-specific

**Two of the three supported engines will not build a project whose code sits in
`src/`.** This is not a style preference — it is a hard constraint of the engine's
own toolchain:

| `engine.name` | Code root | Why it cannot be `src/` |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `src/` | No constraint — Godot loads from `res://` anywhere under the project root. |
| **Unity** | `Assets/` | Unity compiles **only** `Assets/` and `Packages/`. Code outside them is invisible to the compiler. |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/` | UnrealBuildTool discovers modules under `Source/`; content lives in `Content/`. A module elsewhere is not built. |

**Resolve the code root from `engine.name` before writing any source file.** A
path shown as `src/…` alone is a Godot example: read it as *"the code root"* and
substitute the row above. `src/` is the table's Godot row, not a universal path.

**Tests follow the same rule** — the same compilers decide what they see:

| `engine.name` | Test root | Anywhere else |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `tests/unit/`, `tests/integration/` | — |
| **Unity** | `Assets/Tests/EditMode/`, `Assets/Tests/PlayMode/` | not compiled: "0 tests, Passed" |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/Private/Tests/` | not built: "No automation tests matched" |

Read `tests/unit/[system]/` (or `integration/`) anywhere as the test root plus `[System]/`.

# Agent Coordination Rules

1. **Vertical Delegation**: Leadership agents delegate to department leads, who
   delegate to specialists. Never skip a tier for complex decisions.
2. **Horizontal Consultation**: Agents at the same tier may consult each other
   but must not make binding decisions outside their domain.
3. **Conflict Resolution**: When two agents disagree, escalate to the shared
   parent. If no shared parent, escalate to `creative-director` for design
   conflicts or `technical-director` for technical conflicts.
4. **Change Propagation**: When a design change affects multiple domains, the
   `producer` agent coordinates the propagation.
5. **No Unilateral Cross-Domain Changes**: An agent must never modify files
   outside its designated directories without explicit delegation.
6. **Read Design Docs by Section**: A brief names the sections an agent needs
   by heading. Find a heading in a GDD, ADR or the art bible with the Grep
   tool (`^#`, content mode) and Read that range with offset and limit; read a doc
   whole only when the task needs all of it, and say why. `validate-read.sh`
   refuses a whole-file read of a doc over 40 KB.
7. **Nothing Goes Upstream**: Never file, open or comment on an issue or pull
   request in an engine, plugin or vendor repository, even when asked. Write a
   draft (`/bug-report` drafts only) and the user submits it.

## Model Tier Assignment

Read `.claude/docs/model-tiers.md` on demand. It carries the tier table, the
per-skill assignments and the authoring rule.

**Key point:** whether a skill's `model:` is used
depends on how the skill starts. Typed as `/skill-name`: yes, except a `haiku`
pin in auto mode. Started by Claude through the Skill tool: no. Never tell a
user a `haiku` skill saves money; an `opus` skill typed in a Sonnet session
costs more. The agent-side `model:` is a different mechanism, and is applied.

## Subagents vs Agent Teams

This project uses two distinct multi-agent patterns:

### Subagents (current, always active)
Spawned via the `Agent` tool within a single Claude Code session. Used by all
`team-*` skills and orchestration skills. Subagents share the session's
permission context, run sequentially or in parallel within the session, and
return results to the parent.

**When to spawn in parallel**: If two subagents' inputs are independent (neither
needs the other's output to begin), spawn both `Agent` calls simultaneously
rather than waiting. Example: `/review-all-gdds` **Phase 2** (consistency) and
**Phase 3** (design theory) are independent — spawn both at the same time.
Phase 1 loads the GDDs and both depend on it, so it is the one phase here that
must NOT be parallelised.

### Agent Teams (experimental — opt-in)
Multiple independent Claude Code *sessions* coordinated via a shared task list.
Opt-in only — read `.claude/docs/agent-teams.md` on demand before proposing one.

## Parallel Task Protocol

When an orchestration skill spawns multiple independent agents:

1. Issue all independent `Agent` calls before waiting for any result
2. Collect all results before proceeding to dependent phases
3. If any agent is BLOCKED, surface it immediately — do not silently skip
4. Always produce a partial report if some agents complete and others block

# Coding Standards

- All game code must include doc comments on public APIs
- Architecture decisions are recorded as ADRs in `docs/architecture/`. **How many is
  set by `modes.workflow`** — all ADRs at `full`, *critical* ADRs only at `standard`,
  and none required at `minimal`, where the decision log and `design/game-brief.md`
  carry the rationale instead. See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.
- Gameplay values must be data-driven (external config), never hardcoded
- All public methods must be unit-testable (dependency injection over singletons)
- Commits must reference the relevant design document or task ID
- **Commit messages**: Use Conventional Commits format — `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`. Reference the story or task ID in the body (e.g., `Story: EPIC-001-S02`).
- **Verification-driven development**: Write tests first when adding gameplay systems.
  For UI changes, verify with screenshots. Compare expected output to actual output
  before marking work complete. Every implementation should have a way to prove it works.
- **A parse check is not a run.** Every story that changes something
  player-observable is launched and observed before it closes, and the
  observation is a retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/`. Procedure
  per engine: `.claude/docs/run-and-observe.md`. Not waived at
  `qa.level: minimal` — tests are, the look is not.

# Design Document Standards

- All design docs use Markdown
- Each mechanic has a dedicated document in `design/gdd/`
- **How many of the 8 sections are required depends on `modes.workflow`** —
  all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system defines numeric rules — rates,
  curves, thresholds, costs; the system's `Category` is a hint, not the test) at
  `standard`, and no
  GDD at all at `minimal`, where `design/game-brief.md` is the design record.
  See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`. The 8 sections:
  1. **Overview** -- one-paragraph summary
  2. **Player Fantasy** -- intended feeling and experience
  3. **Detailed Rules** -- unambiguous mechanics
  4. **Formulas** -- all math defined with variables
  5. **Edge Cases** -- unusual situations handled
  6. **Dependencies** -- other systems listed
  7. **Tuning Knobs** -- configurable values identified
  8. **Acceptance Criteria** -- testable success conditions
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale

# Testing Standards

## Test Evidence by Story Type

All stories must have appropriate test evidence before they can be marked Done:

| Story Type | Required Evidence | Location | Default Gate Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Logic** (formulas, AI, state machines) | Automated unit test — must pass | `tests/unit/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Integration** (multi-system) | Integration test OR documented playtest | `tests/integration/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Visual/Feel** (animation, VFX, feel) | Retained screenshot + lead sign-off | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **UI** (menus, HUD, screens) | Retained screenshot of each screen touched | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **Config/Data** (balance tuning) | Smoke check pass | `production/qa/smoke-[date].md` | ADVISORY |

The **Default Gate Level** applies when `testing.strict` is not set in
`project.yaml`. A project may override it per test type: `testing.strict.logic`,
`.integration`, `.visual`, `.ui`, and `.config` each take `true` (BLOCKING) or
`false` (ADVISORY). `/story-done`, `/story-readiness`, `/dev-story`,
`/gate-check`, and `/smoke-check` resolve the effective level from that setting,
falling back to the defaults above when it is absent.

> **Why Visual and UI block.** "Retained" is load-bearing — the screenshot must
> still be on disk in `production/qa/evidence/` when the story is closed. One
> that was captured and discarded is an assertion, not evidence. These two rows
> block because for a game the way it looks *is* the product: an advisory visual
> gate gets deferred in favour of whatever does block, and the result is a
> well-tested game that looks wrong.

> **Exception — `/smoke-check`.** The ADVISORY default for **Config/Data** above
> applies to *per-story evidence* gates. `/smoke-check` is a build-health gate,
> not a per-story evidence gate, so its own unset default for
> `testing.strict.config` is **BLOCKING**. The two defaults differ on purpose.

## Automated Test Rules

- **Naming**: per engine — `.claude/rules/test-standards.md`
- **Determinism**: Tests must produce the same result every run — no random seeds, no time-dependent assertions
- **Isolation**: Each test sets up and tears down its own state; tests must not depend on execution order
- **No hardcoded data**: Test fixtures use constant files or factory functions, not inline magic numbers
  (exception: boundary value tests where the exact number IS the point)
- **Independence**: Unit tests do not call external APIs, databases, or file I/O — use dependency injection

## What NOT to Automate

- Visual fidelity (shader output, VFX appearance, animation curves)
- "Feel" qualities (input responsiveness, perceived weight, timing)
- Platform-specific rendering (test on target hardware, not headlessly)
- Full gameplay sessions (covered by playtesting, not automation)

## CI/CD Rules

- Automated test suite runs on every push to main and every PR
- No merge if tests fail — tests are a blocking gate in CI
- Never disable or skip failing tests to make CI pass — fix the underlying issue
- Engine-specific CI commands:
  - **Godot**: `godot --headless -s -d --remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:0 res://addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd -a res://tests --ignoreHeadlessMode`
  - **Unity**: `game-ci/unity-test-runner@v4` (GitHub Actions)
  - **Unreal**: headless runner with `-nullrhi` flag

# Advisor Tool

You have access to an `advisor` tool backed by a stronger reviewer model. It takes NO parameters -- when you call advisor(), your entire conversation history is automatically forwarded. They see the task, every tool call you've made, every result you've seen.

Call advisor BEFORE substantive work -- before writing, before committing to an interpretation, before building on an assumption. If the task requires orientation first (finding files, fetching a source, seeing what's there), do that, then call advisor. Orientation is not substantive work. Writing, editing, and declaring an answer are.

Also call advisor:
- When you believe the task is complete. BEFORE this call, make your deliverable durable: write the file, save the result, commit the change. The advisor call takes time; if the session ends during it, a durable result persists and an unwritten one doesn't.
- When stuck -- errors recurring, approach not converging, results that don't fit.
- When considering a change of approach.

On tasks longer than a few steps, call advisor at least once before committing to an approach and once before declaring done. On short reactive tasks where the next action is dictated by tool output you just read, you don't need to keep calling -- the advisor adds most of its value on the first call, before the approach crystallizes.

Give the advice serious weight. If you follow a step and it fails empirically, or you have primary-source evidence that contradicts a specific claim (the file says X, the paper states Y), adapt. A passing self-test is not evidence the advice is wrong -- it's evidence your test doesn't check what the advice is checking.

If you've already retrieved data pointing one way and the advisor points another: don't silently switch. Surface the conflict in one more advisor call -- "I found X, you suggest Y, which constraint breaks the tie?" The advisor saw your evidence but may have underweighted it; a reconcile call is cheaper than committing to the wrong branch.
</system-reminder>
